book_title: Chapter 7: Why the Stock Trades Here — Market Expectations vs. Peers
question: What growth, margin, and capex normalization is $484.52 already pricing in?

epigraph.quote: Price is what you pay; value is what you get. Every multiple is shorthand for cash-flow durability.
epigraph.author: Institutional Valuation Maxim

web_blocks.title: 7.1 Deconstructing the $3.60 Trillion Market Cap at $484.52

web_blocks.html: At the November 20, 2026 close of $484.52, Microsoft holds a $3,598.14 billion equity market cap across 7.4262 billion implied shares [26]. Enterprise value stands at $3,667.56 billion [26]. That $69.42 billion net debt-and-lease bridge equals $35.48 billion in Q1 carrying debt plus $98.45 billion in on-balance-sheet leases, less $64.51 billion in cash and short-term investments as of September 30, 2026 [31]. On November 4, 2026, Microsoft closed a $25.0 billion 10-tranche senior notes offering [32, 33]. Because cash and debt rose equally, net debt stayed flat while liquidity expanded ahead of peak FY27 spending.

On trailing revenue of $346.44 billion and net income of $142.63 billion ($19.15 TTM EPS), MSFT trades at 25.30x trailing P/E and 20.11x forward P/E [26]. Its PEG ratio sits at 1.02 against 19.64% consensus five-year EPS growth [26]. EV/EBITDA is 17.86x and EV/Sales is 10.59x [26]. A 20.11x forward P/E (4.97% forward earnings yield) sits nearly inline with the 5.04% 10-year US Treasury yield, compressing the equity risk premium cushion.

That multiple compression tracks severe near-term free cash flow dilution. In Q1 FY27, operating cash flow jumped 28.7% YoY to $58.00 billion [31]. Yet cash PP&E additions hit $39.37 billion, component-purchase investing outflows doubled to $12.95 billion, and new finance leases added $5.19 billion [31]. Together, those three outlays totaled $57.51 billion, leaving almost zero economic free cash flow in the quarter. Finviz places trailing P/FCF at 60.01x [26], and Note 12 uncommenced datacenter leases reached $364.6 billion [31].

web_blocks.title: 7.2 Exact 10-Year Reverse DCF & Reconciled Fair Value Estimate

web_blocks.html: With the 10-year US Treasury yield at 5.04% on November 19, 2026, we apply a 9.1% WACC (5.04% risk-free rate, 4.20% equity risk premium, 1.01 beta, and 4.4% after-tax debt cost). We anchor our 10-year unlevered DCF to $346.44 billion TTM revenue, $69.42 billion net debt-plus-leases, and 7.4262 billion diluted shares. Crucially, our model embeds an explicit FY27–FY28 CapEx-and-lease hump: unlevered FCF margins start at 15.0% in Year 1 and 17.0%–17.5% in Year 2 before tapering into steady state by Years 7–10.

Solving that exact 10-year schedule reveals a crucial reality check. Under a 9.1% WACC and 3.5% terminal growth, FCF margins scale from 15.0% to 27.0% steady state. Under that curve, today's $3,667.53B enterprise value ($484.52/share) ALREADY prices in a 13.75% 10-year revenue CAGR. Year 10 revenue hits $1,256.46B with $339.24B in FCF. Discounted cash flows total $1,043.21B and terminal value adds $2,624.32B. Subtracting $69.42B net debt leaves $3,598.11B equity. At $484.52, the margin of safety against consensus is modest.

web_blocks.the_number: $540.00 per share (12-month Base Fair Value). That offers +11.45% upside from $484.52 CMP and a 10.27% discount to fair value.
web_blocks.how_calculated: We blend an exact 10-year Unlevered DCF ($538.12/share) with a 22.5x FY28E EPS multiple ($542.25/share on $24.10 forward EPS). In the DCF, revenue grows at 14.6% CAGR while FCF margins rise from 15.0% to 28.0% at 9.1% WACC and 3.5% terminal growth. Discounted 10-year FCF ($1,133.82B) plus terminal value ($2,931.82B) equals $4,065.63B EV. Subtracting $69.42B net debt and leases leaves $3,996.21B equity across 7.4262B shares.
web_blocks.the_inputs: TTM revenue is $346.44B with $69.42B net debt and leases. Base revenue grows at a 14.6% 10Y CAGR to $1,353.55B in Year 10. Year 1–2 FCF margins sit at 15.0% and 17.5% during peak FY27–28 CapEx. Steady-state FCF margin reaches 28.0% ($378.99B Year 10 FCF) via MAI Code 2 and Cobalt 200 savings.
web_blocks.the_range: Bear fair value sits at $375.00 (12.4% CAGR, 12.5% to 23.5% FCF curve, 9.1% WACC; $2,856.8B EV). Intermediate Stress sits at $448.50 (13.5% CAGR, 25.5% FCF). Base sits at $540.00, and Bull reaches $660.00 (15.9% CAGR, 16.5% to 29.5% FCF, 8.9% WACC; $4,975.5B EV).
web_blocks.if_off: Persistent AI capex plus component outlays could hold terminal FCF margins near 23.5%. If OpenAI concentration also slows revenue CAGR to 12.4%, intrinsic value falls toward $375.00 (-22.6% downside).

Base fair value ($540.00 blend of $538.12 DCF and 22.5x FY28E EPS) offers +11.45% upside vs -22.6% Bear risk ($375.00), making entry price and risk sizing decisive.

web_blocks.title: 7.3 Quantitative Peer Comparison: Hyperscalers & Enterprise Software

web_blocks.html: Comparing Microsoft against listed hyperscalers and software peers clarifies its operational lead and why multiples are compressing. This matrix pulls live November 20, 2026 valuations, margins, and Weinstein stages from the same-session snapshot.

web_blocks.caption: MSFT vs. Hyperscaler & Enterprise Software Peers (Snapshot as of Nov 20, 2026)
web_blocks.takeaway: Snapshot ratings place GOOGL, AMZN, ORCL, and CRM in STAGE_4, though facts_US_2026-11-20.json still tags AMZN ($246.82, just above its $245.15 200-DMA) as Stage 3 while below its 50-DMA ($255.03) and 30W SMA ($254.95). MSFT holds the highest OPM (47.1%) and avoids Stage 4, yet trades at 20.11x forward P/E against 9x–23x peers.

web_blocks.html: Relative multiples confirm that Stage 4 peer compression caps near-term multiple expansion. Alphabet trades at 13.85x trailing P/E (17.73x forward). Oracle trades at 15.86x trailing P/E (9.12x forward) after a 56% one-year selloff. Salesforce trades at 16.47x trailing P/E (11.25x forward). Note the minor data divergence on Amazon. Our snapshot labels AMZN STAGE_4 because $246.82 sits below its 30-week SMA ($254.95) and 50-day SMA ($255.03). Meanwhile, facts_US_2026-11-20.json classifies AMZN as Stage 3 because it remains +0.68% above its 200-day SMA ($245.15). Against that cautious peer group, re-rating to 25.5x forward earnings looks unrealistic. Our 22.5x FY28E EPS assumption ($542.25) aligns cleanly with our $538.12 DCF.

Ignite 2026 product launches remain essential to hitting that 28.0% terminal FCF margin in our Base DCF. Replacing third-party frontier model calls inside Copilot and GitHub with proprietary MAI Code 2 (40% of GPT-6.1 Sol cost; 5% of Claude Opus 5.5 cost) and MAI Cyber 2 Flash [39] curbs API royalty drag. Likewise, Cobalt 200 custom ARM silicon lowers internal compute cost across 23 Azure regions [37, 38], helping offset Q1 D&A acceleration (+44.2% YoY).

web_blocks.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION — Respecting Honest DCF Gravity
paragraphs: Running the exact 10-year DCF with a 5.04% Treasury yield and an explicit FY27–28 CapEx hump removes false comfort. At $484.52, the market already expects 13.75% annual revenue growth and 27% terminal FCF margins. Base fair value of $540.00 offers +11.45% upside against -22.6% Bear risk ($375.00)—meaning price discipline matters more than ever.

web_blocks.html: Valuation Trigger: We cut Base fair value toward $448.50–$375.00 if Microsoft Cloud gross margin breaks 62%, FY28E CapEx+leases remain above 30% of sales, or OpenAI receivables ($7.2B) require material write-downs.

book_paragraphs: Now that we have completed our price-blind audit—and uncovered the $12.95 billion in quarterly component purchases, $364.6 billion in uncommenced datacenter leases, and $10.0 billion in single-quarter OpenAI revenue—let us confront the live November 20, 2026 market price with rigorous math. Microsoft closed at $484.52 per share, giving it a $3.60 trillion equity value and a $3.67 trillion enterprise value after adding $35.48 billion in debt and $98.45 billion in on-balance-sheet leases and subtracting $64.51 billion in cash.

At $484.52, Microsoft trades at 25.30 times trailing earnings and 20.11 times forward earnings. On the surface, twenty times forward earnings for an 18.8 percent grower with 47.1 percent operating margins looks cheap compared to 2021. Yet two forces explain why the market compressed the multiple: free cash flow dilution and a 5.04 percent 10-year US Treasury yield. In Q1 fiscal 2027, operating cash flow surged to $58.0 billion, but $39.4 billion in cash capex, $12.95 billion in component-purchase outflows, and $5.19 billion in new finance leases absorbed $57.5 billion, leaving near-zero economic free cash flow for the quarter.

When we run an exact 10-year unlevered Reverse DCF—using a 9.1 percent cost of capital anchored to that 5.04 percent Treasury yield and modeling a real FY27–FY28 capex hump where FCF margins start at 15 percent before tapering toward 27 percent—we uncover a sobering truth. Today's $484.52 share price already implies a 13.75 percent ten-year revenue growth rate, taking sales from $346 billion today to $1.26 trillion in Year 10. In other words, the current stock price is not pricing in stagnation; it already expects world-class compounding.

That disciplined DCF math forces us to lower our Base fair value cleanly from prior inflated targets down to $540.00 per share. Exactly how do we get $540.00? In our Base DCF, revenue compounds at 14.6 percent per year on $677 billion in commercial RPO, while MAI Code 2 and Cobalt 200 silicon lift steady-state FCF margins to 28.0 percent—yielding $538.12 per share ($1.13 trillion PV of 10-year cash flows plus $2.93 trillion PV of terminal value, less $69.42 billion net debt and leases, divided by 7.4262 billion shares). Blending that $538.12 DCF with a realistic 22.5 times normalized FY28 earnings multiple ($542.25) anchors our $540.00 Base target—just +11.45 percent upside above $484.52.

Equally important, we stress-test the downside without flinching. If AI capital intensity and component spending stay stubbornly elevated so terminal FCF margins stall at 23.5 percent, and OpenAI concentration slows 10-year revenue compounding to 12.4 percent, our exact DCF drops to $375.35—roughly $375.00 per share, or -22.6 percent downside from today's close. Under an intermediate stress case at 13.5 percent growth and 25.5 percent FCF margin, fair value sits at $448.50. Meanwhile, our Bull case at 15.9 percent growth, 29.5 percent FCF margins, and an 8.9 percent WACC reaches $660.00.

Stacking Microsoft against mega-cap peers shows why a modest 22.5 times exit multiple is the honest ceiling right now. On November 20, Alphabet traded at 17.7 times forward earnings, Salesforce at 11.3 times, and Oracle at 9.1 times—all inside Weinstein Stage 4 downtrends. Even Amazon sat below its 50-day and 30-week averages (Stage 4 in our snapshot, Stage 3 in our market-facts ledger just above its 200-day average). Microsoft deserves a quality premium for its 47.1 percent operating margin and 24.2 percent ROIC, yet when peers trade between 9 times and 23 times forward earnings, expecting multiple expansion back to 26 or 30 times is wishful thinking.

Walk through the enterprise-value-to-equity bridge step by step so nothing sits inside a black box. In our Base DCF, discounted free cash flows over Years 1 through 10 contribute $1.13 trillion, while the terminal value discounted at 9.1 percent contributes $2.93 trillion—summing to $4.07 trillion in enterprise value. Subtracting $69.42 billion in net debt and on-balance-sheet leases leaves $4.00 trillion in equity value across 7.4262 billion shares, or $538.12 per share.

Also examine how Ignite 2026 innovations feed directly into that Year 10 margin target. By deploying MAI Code 2 inside Copilot and GitHub at 40 percent of GPT-6.1 Sol cost and just 5 percent of Claude Opus 5.5 cost, alongside MAI Cyber 2 Flash at under 2 percent of competing API cost and Cobalt 200 ARM servers across 23 regions, Microsoft attacks third-party royalty inflation before it erodes cloud gross margins. Even if accounting depreciation rises $12 billion to $15 billion on shorter GPU useful lives, discounted cash flow tracks cash outlays rather than non-cash GAAP charges.

Look at what that means for your capital. With +11.45 percent upside to our $540.00 Base target and -22.60 percent downside to our $375.00 Bear case, fundamental reward-to-risk at $484.52 is just 0.51-to-1. That narrow valuation cushion is why we cannot treat $484.52 as a pound-the-table bargain—and why both technical support confirmation and strict portfolio weight discipline are mandatory.
